A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InvisibleInk research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting, reordering, and expanded experiments.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original synthetic-text generation experiments, baseline comparisons, and ablations on MIMIC, Yelp, and TAB.

after.justification: V2 retains original generation experiments and reports additional downstream classification results, revised ablations, and expanded scaling results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same DClip aggregation, public-logit vocabulary expansion, and exponential-mechanism sampling. Expanded explanations, software examples, and the supplementary disclaimer-removal analysis do not establish a change to the proposed generation procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds a distinct downstream learning task: training RoBERTa on synthetic Yelp reviews and evaluating 50-class category/rating classification on real test data. The original three generation datasets remain; the MIMIC-IV-Note naming correction does not establish different data coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds public generation as a comparator across the MIMIC utility–compute panels, including perplexity, length, and medical-entity counts. V1 reported public-generation MAUVE separately. The principal private comparators—Amin et al., AdaPMixED, and AugPE—remain.

E3.justification: V2 switches the main AdaPMixED comparisons from add-or-remove to replace-by-null adjacency and changes the reported ΔPPL aggregation. Main truncated MIMIC results change from k=50, temperature 1.2 to k=100, temperature 1.1. LLaMA3-8B generation counts increase from 500 to 1000 with expanded parameter coverage, and the downstream classifier introduces a new training/evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Existing sensitivity studies are extended with joint temperature/top-k sweeps in new Figure 10 and an additional privacy-budget case in Figure 6. Appendix E.3 adds a targeted analysis of removing disclaimers from LLaMA3-8B outputs. Earlier clipping and adjacency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 describes 99% Wald intervals over generated samples without specifying repeated-run counts. V2 explicitly reports three-run means with 95% intervals for major MIMIC figures and tables, and identifies several other evaluations as single-run. Appendix D.6 adds the 95% coefficient but retains its general 99% wording, leaving some reporting ambiguity.

E6.justification: Main MIMIC scores and curves are revised, and the former LLaMA3-8B Table 3 becomes expanded Table 13 under different sample counts. New Table 3 reports Yelp classification accuracies of 32.98%, 29.44%, and 7.44% for InvisibleInk, Amin et al., and AdaPMixED at epsilon=10 and B=7, 127, and 31 respectively. The adjacency appendix also replaces TLE with 58.80 at epsilon=3, B=128 under replace-by-null adjacency.

T1.justification: Appendix D.4 changes ΔPPL from the mean of per-text absolute deviations to the absolute difference of corpus mean perplexities; these definitions are inequivalent. Appendix B.3.2 also reformulates data-dependent privacy using null replacement instead of deletion. The main sensitivity bounds, composition proofs, and Theorem 2 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central framework and privacy–utility–compute contributions remain. V2 sharpens the headline non-private overhead claim to 4–8×, adds a 'for the first time' qualification, and foregrounds the released software package. V1 stated less than 10× in the abstract and less than 8× in the conclusion.

C2.justification: V1's positive scaling discussion gains an important qualification: v2 attributes weaker LLaMA3-8B medical generation to alignment and disclaimers. V2 also warns that downstream classification can reward keywords without coherent text, and explicitly limits reported privacy guarantees to a single hyperparameter setting rather than accounting for tuning. These additions materially qualify utility and applicability.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release; v2 reports released experimental code and the invink package, with installation instructions and a worked API example in Appendix F explaining batch_size versus B. V2 also discloses the AdaPMixED brentq solver, classifier training hyperparameters, and a corrected MIMIC-IV-Note access location.

R1.justification: Related work adds a focused discussion of public-data priors in private tabular synthesis and citations covering DP-Fusion, textual sanitization, and decoding hyperparameters. The principal positioning relative to private inference, API-access methods, and concurrent work is retained. Bibliographic publication updates do not constitute new cited research.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites selected explanations of prior-method drawbacks and Top-k+ sampling, rearranges related-work paragraphs, and reorganizes the experimental discussion. Scaling discussion moves into Appendix E.3, and a software appendix is added. The overall narrative and most theoretical exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different conference layout and substantially revises empirical displays, including reordered Table 2 columns, confidence-interval notation, new legends, and expanded plot panels. It adds the Top-k+ schematic, downstream-results table, and joint parameter-sweep figure, while relocating and expanding the scaling table.

improvement.justification: The downstream test and explicit three-run MIMIC reporting substantially strengthen validation beyond v1's generation-quality evaluation and unspecified run counts. Matching AdaPMixED's adjacency and documenting released software address comparison and reproducibility gaps, while new limitations improve interpretation. Reporting inconsistencies remain, including Table 2's 36-hour timeout versus Appendix D.7's 24-hour description, but they do not outweigh these substantial gains.
